Subject: Request: temporary SLA variation for P1/P2 coverage

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding help last week. We have a tight launch window for our caregiver triage feature (week of Mar 1) and one item popped up in our readiness review — our internal ops team needs guaranteed 24/7 P1 on-call coverage with a 30 minute response SLA.

We understand Redwood's standard P1 response for our tier is 30 minutes during business hours and 1 hour on weekends. Given the risk profile of the clinical workflow, we need to request a temporary SLA exception to ensure a consistent 30 minute P1 response across the full launch window (expected 8 weeks), and P2 response to be tightened to 2 hours.

We are willing to sign a short amendment to the SOW and provide additional credits if needed. Can you confirm if Redwood can accommodate a timeboxed exception and what operational changes would be needed on your side?

Appreciate a quick turn here — we need internal confirmation by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Clinical Ops
Valerian Health

Samira — thanks for flagging and for the context. We can absolutely evaluate a timeboxed exception. My read: acceptable operational path would be a 60-day (8-week) exception with explicit on-call adjustments, monitoring commitments, and a signed SOW amendment. 

High-level proposal from my side (pending internal sign-off):
- P1 response: 30 minutes (24/7) for 8 weeks
- P2 response: 2 hours
- Redwood to provide dedicated on-call rotation coverage for Valerian during launch window (staffed by dedicated support engineers)
- Mandatory alerting/playbook and runbook updates on both sides
- Timeboxed amendment to SOW + DocuSign for legal

I am looping in Vivek, Monica, and Priyom to confirm operational feasibility and legal acceptance. I will aim to get an internal decision today so we can finalize wording for the amendment.

—Laura

Thanks Laura. Operational notes and constraints:

- We can support a dedicated 24/7 P1 rotation for the 8-week window, staffed by two senior on-call engineers plus a senior support lead as escalation. I estimate a marginal cost of ~2.5 FTE-weeks across the window (we'll staff from our overtime pool).
- To meet 30 minute P1 response across weekends, we'll put engineers into a split-weekend rotation (attached: oncall_schedule_proposal.xlsx).
- We will require: clear alerting thresholds (error rate upticks, latency > X ms, request-error spikes), a Valerian incident contact list, and an agreed playbook for triage and mitigation.
- For P2 (2 hours), we can extend standard triage workflows and commit to status updates every 30 minutes until mitigated.
- Operational risk: if we observe sustained yearly rolling incidents or repeated infrastructure overloads, we reserve the right to trigger an emergency rollback to default SLOs (but we will notify Valerian 24 hours in advance if possible).

Next steps I need from you (Laura / Samira):

2) Sign-off on on-call schedule and amendment language by Feb 17

Attaching the schedule and a draft runbook stub.

We can approve a timeboxed amendment with the following legal guardrails:
- 60-day exception (with a 2-week extension option if both parties agree in writing)
- No change to underlying warranties or liability caps — we will not accept broad new indemnities tied to patient outcomes; any clinical-risk language must be narrow and factual
- Add a requirement for a joint incident postmortem for any P1 incident during the exception window

I will prepare an amendment draft and a DocuSign envelope; sending to Laura for commercial terms and to Samira for counter-signature. Please note: add a clause that Redwood may suspend the exception if abuse or repeated incidents occur (Monica's emergency rollback note).
